entityDescription:
The University of Craiova is a Romanian public institution of higher education, founded in 1947, functioning ever since, gaining experience and importance every year. Counting around 2,000 staff members and 25,000 students, it is one of the biggest higher education institutions in Romania. 
The university offers a wide field of Bachelor and Master Programs in sciences, polytechnic engineering, agriculture, humanities, social studies, economics, law, theology and arts (33 specializations and 66 diplomas). The University of Craiova organises Ph.D. Programs in over 70 fields. The institution undertakes major responsibilities in scientific research and in widening active and adequate participation to the social life. The scientific events, the promotion of science, culture and education alongside the cultural events organised by the university make it attractive to different age groups. In this respect, ones of its main priorities are related to research on climate changes and to youngster education in environmental protection. Its main contribution is related to: (i) participation in large-scale EU research projects, within FP7 or Horizon 2020, (ii) publication of a large number of monographs and scientific papers in well known national and international journals, (iii) initiation and organisation of numerous scientific events involving the national and international communities of practice. 
The participation of the University of Craiova in the proposed WASTE Project could combine the expertises of various groups of researchers and educators, focusing on the identification of success measures of environmental protection, of employability enhancing factors, of active citizenship, of establishing virtual communities of practice/social connectivity etc.

SpaceLayer Tech. a spinoff of University of Coimbra and PRIMALAYER, a GIS company has been established in 2015 under the ESA-BIC Portugal initiative for the downstream use of space assets in non-space environment. Based at Portugal it reached profitability in 2017 in the public sector for the use of analytics in Civil Protection platforms. entityDescription: Stowarzyszenie Naukowe Archeologów Polskich (SNAP) is officially recognised, biggest Polish NGO grouping archaeologists and specialists in related fields, including active scientists as well as officials of the state administration dealing with the protection of cultural heritage. SNAP closely cooperates with Ministry of Culture and National Heritage. Our mission is scientific research in the field of archaeology as well as protection and promotion of cultural (archaeological) heritage. Warsaw Department of SNAP plays key role within the federal structure of the organisation. Both SNAP as a federation, and Warsaw Department in particular took part in numerous projects concerning research and protection of archaeological heritage, including non-invasive methods of detection by aerial imaging and LIDAR – based numeric terrain modelling. Most of the project were financed by the Ministry of Culture and National Heritage Board of Poland. The participation in Atlas project is fully compliant with the SNAP mission and its former and present experiences.

IMDEA Nanociencia is a non-profit Foundation created on November 23rd 2006 by initiative of the regional Government of the Community of Madrid in November 2006 in order to shorten the distance between the research and society in the Madrid region and provide new capacity for research, technological development and innovation in the field of Nanoscience, Nanotechnology and Molecular Design. In 2007 the former Ministry of Education and Science of the Government of Spain decided to also fund part of the creation and equipment of an institute of Nanoscience in the Community of Madrid.
The Foundation manages the IMDEA Nanociencia Institute, a new interdisciplinary research Centre dedicated to the exploration of basic nanoscience and the development of applications of nanotechnology in connection with innovative industries. The IMDEA Nanociencia Institute is part of one of the strategic lines of the Campus of International Excellence (CEI) UAM+CSIC.

entityDescription: Founded as a branch of The National Institute of Research and Development for Biological Sciences (NIRDBS), we are dedicated to research in microorganisms, plant and animal biology. We combine traditional and modern molecular biology methods in studying biodiversity and developing strategies for sustainable exploitation of resources. This involves studies of ecology, taxonomy, and phylogeny on cyanobacteria, algae, invertebrates, and higher plants. We also conduct research on more applied aspects of life sciences, like energy production using microorganisms, synthesis of biological compounds in culture media, in-vitro multiplication of plant species for repopulation purposes, or production of new maize hybrids.

The Department of Environment (DoE), of the Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment (MARDE) is the consulting body for environmental policy issues and coordinator of environment related projects/ programmes. Additionally, the DoE constitutes the national focal point of several intergovernmental organizations such as UNFCCC, CSD, MCSD, SMAP, MAP, INFOTERRA and UNEP, and of various Conventions such as the CITES, the Bern Convention, the Barcelona Convention, the Basel Convention, the Ramsar Convention, the Aarhus Convention, the Vienna Convention etc.
The DoE is also responsible for implementation of the Habitats Directive, as well as the protection and management of Natura 2000 network in Cyprus. It employs professionals on environmental management, natural sciences, pollution control, geology and marine ecology.

entityDescription:
Warwickshire Wildlife Trust aims to protect and enhance wildlife, natural habitats and geology throughout Warwickshire, Coventry and Solihull, and to encourage a greater awareness, appreciation and participation in all aspects of nature conservation and the environment.

We are the leading local conservation charity with over 23,000 members dedicated to supporting our vital work for nature conservation across the county. 

Warwickshire Wildlife Trust is working to create a Living Landscape by:
Managing Nature Reserves - with 65 nature reserves spanning 800 hectares across Warwickshire, a large portion of our role is the management of these havens for wildlife and people. Find out more about nature reserves in Warwickshire.

Engaging our communities to enjoy and care for wildlife - We work on projects at the heart of communities to help build positive relationships between people and their natural spaces.

Encouraging and supporting volunteers - we are indebted to the 500 plus volunteers who help us in every aspect of our work from conservation through to administration. This is why we are committed to being as supportive and inclusive to each dedicated individual.

Educating people about nature - We provide educational activities to thousands of children every year as well as guided walks, talks and events for people of all ages.

Campaigning on behalf of the environment - We are there to give a strong local voice in helping to protect threatened places and rare species.

entityDescription: Orbitile sp. z o.o. is a start-up based in Warsaw, Poland. The idea behind it, is to use the possibilities satellite technology brings to answer practical business challenges, particularly for insurance companies and agro agencies. Our team has expertise in all areas that we believe are crucial for success: Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, IT & AI and business development. As we work closely with academies, we have broad network of scientists who agreed to share their expertise with us when needed. Orbitile is very much business oriented, however we are open to challenging research projects as well, as taking part in such helps us stay up-to-date and it is particularly motivating for the team.
